Thank you, Hitul. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. This wasn't a 
typical quarter, but I am very proud of how our teams and partners handled it to deliver a very 
strong performance. As you know, there have been some regulatory changes that have 
impacted the market volumes. 
 
However, as we have always maintained, regulatory changes are designed to make our markets 
stronger, even if sometimes the refinement and the ecosystem adjusting to it may take time. 
You saw a bit of it this quarter. However, the Indian capital markets and the economy continue 
to be strong with the GDP growing at 7.8% last quarter. No mean feat at this scale. 
 
As I mentioned earlier, I am very proud that our users, partners and teams adapted fast. In 
September, average daily orders rebounded to 5.8 million, up nearly 12% from August. Despite 
the regulatory environment, our consolidated revenue and PAT grew 18.9% and 58.2% year-
over-year, respectively.

1.5 million new clients this quarter, 11.6% more than Q1, and we did it while keeping 
acquisition costs well under control. We also witnessed growth in our NSE active client base, 
leading to an expansion in our active clients market share month-over-month in each month 
of this quarter. 
 
And here's another interesting number you'd like to take away. Our average client funding book 
reached a lifetime high of ₹ 74.5 billion, up about 40.5% from a year ago. Our overall equity 
retail market share based on option premium turnover stood at 19.7%. In the derivatives, we 
held our position with a retail turnover share of 22.1% for the quarter, and it rose to 22.5% in 
September, even as our market share in cash moderated. 
 
In commodities, our turnover more than doubled over last year. Our share came down to 44% 
because of market expansion owing to more participants entering the market, which is a sign 
of how fast the segment is growing. We are one of the leading players now in a much bigger 
market.  
On investing, our SIP registrations grew nearly 12% over Q1. For many of our clients, mutual 
funds becomes the first engagement on the platform. 
 
Credit is where I'm especially excited. Responsible credit is a tremendous opportunity for India, 
and the journey is just getting started. In September, we delivered our highest ever credit 
distribution, taking our annualized run rate to ₹ 33 billion. That is powered by continuous 
advances in our AI and ML capabilities. Our credit models run on a continuous data flywheel of 
learning, iteration and refinement. This helps us sharpen risk assessment, making sure that we 
show loan offers to the appropriate cohorts, reducing risk for consumers as well as our lending 
partners. We upgraded our probability of default model and launched the early beta of our 
loan against securities offering. As we have always guided, we will scale this business with 
discipline and responsibility. With a client base of this size, the opportunity in front of us is very 
large. 
Our wealth business is gaining depth as well with Ionic Wealth AUM at ₹ 160 billion, up 19.1% 
over Q1 FY27. The regulatory backdrop is also turning positive supportive with SEBI's Board 
approving new portfolio manager regulations. A wider product shelf means platforms like ours 
can offer clients richer, more diversified portfolios.

authorization to operate as a Global Access Provider in the IFSC. With that, we are piloting U.S. 
stocks on our platform. We are excited about providing a simple way for our users to access 
the largest market in the world.

the aim to lower insurance costs, thus bringing the product within reach of many more Indians. 
It's still a proposal, but we believe a lower cost, more transparent model is good for the 
consumers and favors digital platforms like ours, which can reach clients at scale and add 
insurance to the financial relationships we are already building. 
 
What ties this together is our technology capabilities and a platform built to be product 
agnostic. We can go deeper across capital markets, wealth, credit and other financial services. 
Each addition deepens the relationship, raises lifetime value and unlocks operating leverage 
without a proportionate rise in cost, and that compounds across customer economics, 
profitability and enterprise value. 
 
Now AI. For us, it's becoming a shared intelligence layer across the group, embedded in our 
business, products and operations. For customers, it makes discovery, engagement, support 
and personalization better. Inside the company, it speeds up productivity, automation and 
decision-making across functions. 
 
All of these sit with a strong governance and security framework, which is critical as we scale 
the AI-first operating model because security and trust are non-negotiable. This quarter, we 
strengthened our cybersecurity stack with AI-driven vulnerability detection and automated 
remediation workflows, improving our resilience and reducing risk exposure.

clients, orders recovering, stand-alone margins above the upper end of our range and a credit 
business that's starting to scale further. India's financial journey is a long one. We are building 
Angel One to be with our clients every step of the way in this journey. Thank you.

closing book reached a record ₹ 82.1 billion. Importantly, the number of funded clients 
increased by nearly 30% over the last year to 437,000, reflecting broader client adoption. 
 
Distribution income also recorded healthy growth, supported by strong credit distribution and 
IPO activity. The increasing contribution from these businesses is progressively broadening our 
earnings base and enabling us to monetize our growing client franchise beyond transaction-led 
income. 
 
Moving to profitability. Consolidated operating margins stood at 45.1% compared to 34.5% in 
the corresponding quarter last year, an expansion of over 1,000 basis points. At the stand-alone 
level, operating margins reached 48.9%, exceeding our guided range of 40% to 45%. 
 
Importantly, after normalizing for seasonal IPL expenditure and ESOP-related reversals, 
consolidated operating margins remained stable at 43.8% compared to 43.6% in the preceding 
quarter. This stability in underlying margins despite softer trading activity and continued 
investment in growth reinforces our confidence in the operating efficiency and scalability of 
our business. 
 
While quarterly margins will naturally fluctuate depending on market activity, seasonality and 
the timing of investments, we remain confident in our ability to sustain stand-alone operating 
margins of around 45% on an annual basis. 
 
This provides us with the flexibility to continue investing in future growth opportunities while 
maintaining a healthy balance between growth and profitability. Coming to our balance sheet. 
Net worth increased to ₹ 67.1 billion compared with ₹ 58.3 billion a year ago. 
 
Borrowings stood at approximately ₹ 75.5 billion, largely reflecting the expansion of our client 
funding portfolio. The underlying portfolio remains granular and well collateralized. 
Approximately 84% of clients -- funded clients have exposures below ₹ 100,000, while 82% of 
the closing book is less than 30 days old.

several quarters, we have been steadily strengthening our earnings capacity of our business 
through an expanding revenue base, deeper client monetization and improved operating

largely incurred upfront, while existing customer cohorts continue to contribute revenues over 
time with relatively low incremental servicing costs. 
 
As customer relationships mature and product adoption deepens, this creates meaningful 
opportunities for incremental earnings and operating leverage. What is particularly reassuring 
is that we are seeing the benefits of this model even during periods of relative subdued trading 
activity. 
 
As market conditions become more supportive, we believe our broader earnings base and 
scalable operating infrastructure position us well to capture incremental opportunities and 
translate them efficiently into profitability. 
 
Our financial priorities remain clear, maintain healthy margins, strengthen return on capital 
and ensure that our investments translate into sustainable long-term shareholder value. 
Overall, Q2 reinforces our confidence in the financial strength, scalability and long-term 
earnings potential of Angel One.
